listing_view.reasoning: Subscription reached only ~1.52x by mid-day on the final day after sitting near zero for most of the window, which is lukewarm demand for a mainboard IPO. The offer is heavily secondary (~₹2,880mn of the ₹3,680mn is not fresh issue, per the fresh_issue vs issue_size figures), so existing holders are cashing out at ~47x earnings with no grey-market or anchor data to suggest pricing support.

longterm_view.reasoning: Growth and margins are genuinely improving (EBITDA margin 6.9% to 11.3%, PAT up sharply) and leverage is modest (debt/equity ~0.25). But earnings convert poorly to cash (~0.35 of EBITDA, FCF only ₹105mn in the latest year), receivable days are climbing (66.8 to 82.5), and 37% of incremental sales is uncollected money — the quality of the recent profit jump is unproven.

governance.reasoning: Positive: no shares pledged or encumbered as of the document date [capital_structure, page 135] and no pending regulatory action against promoters is disclosed [litigation, page 471]. However the extracts contain no detail on related-party transaction scale or promoter conduct beyond boilerplate, so this is a neutral-not-clean score.

key_risks.risk: Weak cash conversion despite profit surge
key_risks.why_it_matters: Only ~35% of EBITDA arrived as operating cash in the latest year, so reported earnings growth may not fund the business or dividends.
Receivable days rose from 66.8 to 82.5 and 37% of incremental revenue is uncollected, suggesting channel stuffing or weakening customer quality.
Only ₹800mn of the ~₹3,680mn issue is fresh capital; most proceeds go to sellers, not the company's growth.
The prospectus itself flags dependence on its manufacturing facility and stringent environmental/labour compliance as material risks [business, page 310; business, page 318].

answers.question: check receivables and inventory against the sales growth
answers.answer: Receivables are outpacing sales: revenue grew ~21.7% in the latest year but receivable days stretched from 71.1 to 82.5, and 37% of the incremental revenue is money not yet collected — consistent with the weak operating cash flow (₹494.7mn against ₹1,393mn EBITDA). Inventory cannot be checked; no inventory figure is given in the figures or extracts.

answers.question: who is selling, and how much of their stake?
answers.answer: Partly answerable: arithmetically ~₹2,880mn of the ₹3,680mn offer is an offer for sale (fresh issue is only ₹800mn), so selling shareholders are offloading roughly 78% of the issue. But the extracts do not name the selling shareholders or state what percentage of their holdings they are selling, so identity and stake-sold fraction cannot be established from what I was given.

answer.what_would_change_my_mind: Evidence that the OFS sellers are financial investors exiting fully (rather than promoters trimming), plus one more year of operating cash flow tracking EBITDA and receivable days stabilising, would turn me constructive. Conversely, clarity that the recent margin jump came from a cyclical chemical price upswing would push the long-term view lower.
